official_measurement_examples.name: SSSI boundary dataset
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's SSSI dataset represents land notified as an SSSI under the Wildlife and Countryside Act and does not include proposed sites.

official_measurement_examples.name: Impact Risk Zone role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's SSSI Impact Risk Zones are a GIS screening tool for local planning authorities to identify development types that may affect SSSIs and when Natural England consultation may be needed.

official_measurement_examples.name: IRZ not automatic refusal
official_measurement_examples.fact: An Impact Risk Zone intersection indicates a need for further consideration or consultation according to proposal type; it is not itself proof that a project damages an SSSI or must be refused.

official_measurement_examples.name: Public-body assent scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Public bodies must seek Natural England assent before carrying out activities likely to damage SSSI special interest, including relevant activities outside the site boundary that could cause damage.

official_measurement_examples.name: Third-party permission advice
official_measurement_examples.fact: A public body considering permission for a third party activity likely to damage SSSI special interest must seek Natural England statutory advice before giving that permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Owner occupier consent route
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's April 2026 guidance provides a separate consent-advice route for owners or occupiers proposing activities on SSSI land.

official_measurement_examples.name: SSSI Units distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's SSSI Units dataset divides designated SSSIs for condition and management recording; units are management subdivisions rather than separate SSSI designations.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning and protected-site separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning permission, SSSI assent or consent, Habitats Regulations assessment and other environmental permits are separate controls and must not be inferred from one another.

core_rules: SSSI boundary data is designation evidence not a complete planning decision
SSSI Impact Risk Zone data is screening evidence not SSSI designation
an IRZ intersection is not automatic proof of adverse effect
absence from an IRZ trigger is not a general environmental clearance
SSSI assent is not planning permission
planning permission is not SSSI assent or consent
owner or occupier SSSI consent is distinct from public-body assent
activities outside an SSSI boundary can still require assessment if they may damage special interest
SSSI Unit boundaries are management subdivisions not separate designations
protected-species licensing is distinct from SSSI site protection
Habitats Regulations assessment is distinct from SSSI assent even where sites overlap
air-pollution screening must retain project emissions and protected-feature scope
historic SSSI condition evidence must retain unit date and assessment context
SSSI compliance does not determine land ownership access rights or development capacity
no parcel SSSI clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
